backbone.rule: A work is on the backbone when a pollution-core v0 term matches its title or abstract: whole word, case-insensitive, plural allowed (atlas.review_highlight.term_pattern). This is a local check on the raw pages, not OpenAlex's stemmed search, so it can differ slightly from it.

caps.component_rule: Largest connected component of the edge graph (ties: the component with the smallest institution id), then the top nodes by works (ties by id) within it.
caps.edge_rule: Edges come from backbone works with 2 to 25 distinct authors; weight is the number of shared works. Works above the cap add to node works only.
caps.name_rule: display_name is the public OpenAlex author name from the latest page holding the author. country_code is the most frequent institution country over the author's backbone authorships (each authorship counts each country once; ties: lowest code); null when none.
caps.names_are_public: names are public OpenAlex author names
caps.thinning_rule: Per node keep its k strongest edges (ties: the other node's works, then id) and keep the union. If over budget, drop weight-1 edges (last index first) that leave both ends with an edge. If still over budget, lower k by one and repeat. Desktop: budget 60,000 edges, k starts at 8. Phone: budget 15,000, k starts at 3, applied to the phone subset alone. Every node keeps its strongest edge. Communities and layout use the thinned desktop graph.

author_graph.what_this_is_and_is_not: Co-authorship graph of OpenAlex authors on the pollution-core backbone: unscreened global query hits whose title or abstract contain a pollution-core v0 term (A3 section 5.3). A node is an author; an edge joins two authors who share a backbone work, and its weight is the number of such works. It is not a screened corpus and not a measure of research quality. Names are public OpenAlex author names (owner decision 2026-11-25). No emails, raw affiliation strings, ORCIDs or abstracts are written. Works with more than 25 authors count toward node works but add no edges. Only the largest connected component is kept, then the 20,000 authors with the most backbone works (and the edges among them). The phone file is the first 5,000 of those nodes.

caps.edge_rule: Edges come from works with 2 to 50 distinct institutions; weight is the number of shared works. Works above the cap add to node works only.

Phone: budget 15,000, k starts at 3, applied to the phone subset alone. Every node keeps its strongest edge. Communities and layout use the thinned desktop graph.

authors.community_method: Louvain (networkx) on the weighted kept graph, seed 42; community 0 is the largest.
authors.layout_format: little-endian float32 pairs (x, y) in node order; node i occupies bytes 8*i to 8*i+7. The phone graph uses the first phone-cap entries.
authors.layout_method: ForceAtlas2 (networkx, scaling ratio 10, strong gravity 0.05, node mass 1 + weighted degree) run separately inside each Louvain community for the stated iterations, starting from seeded random points; each community is scaled by the square root of its size and the communities are placed on a sunflower spiral (largest at the centre); the whole layout is scaled to [-1, 1]. Edges between communities do not shape the layout.

authors_phone.layout_entries: the first 5000 entries of the layout file

what_this_is_and_is_not: Institution co-occurrence graph from the unscreened global OpenAlex query hits (plastic query version in this manifest). A node is an institution; an edge joins two institutions that appear on the same work, and its weight is the number of such works. It is not a screened corpus and not a measure of collaboration quality. It holds no person-level data: no author names, author IDs or ORCIDs. Works with more than 50 institutions count toward node works but add no edges. Only the largest connected component is kept, then the 20,000 institutions with the most works (and the edges among them). The phone file is the first 5,000 of those nodes.
